newsitem.title: CHINA: Grocers mistaken for N.Korea agents in China drama.
newsitem.headline: Grocers mistaken for N.Korea agents in China drama.

text.p: Grocery workers collecting money for delivery of beer and rice cakes prompted a scare in Beijing on Tuesday when they were mistaken for Pyongyang agents trying to trick their way into the residence of a top Seoul official.

A report by South Korea's Yonhap news agency, which said three men -- apparently North Koreans -- had harassed the wife of Seoul's consul-general amid a crisis over a Pyongyang official seeking asylum with the South's mission in Beijing, was a false alarm, said Seoul embassy spokesman Chang Moon Ik.
The wife of the consul general had called the embassy in a fright when three Korean men knocked on her door and asked to come in to collect money for delivery of beer and rice cakes, Chang said.
South Korean officials then called the manager of a local Korean grocery store who said the scare was a misunderstanding, Chang said.
"The manager of the supermarket said he sent his men to another apartment and he had misread the address to them," he said.

Hwang Jang-yop, the most senior North Korean to betray his Stalinist homeland, has been holed up for seven days in Seoul's consular compound, which has been heavily guarded by Chinese armoured personnel carriers and squads of armed police.
